The *Ubbaripetavatthu* (Pv 25) is a verse narrative within the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative, an ascetic consoles Queen Ubbari and extinguishes her grief over the loss of a loved one [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].

Curated data on SuttaCentral notes connections between the *Ubbaripetavatthu* and several other canonical and paracanonical texts dealing with consolation and grief, including the *Goṇapetavatthu* (Pv 8), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17), *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83), and five Jātakas: the *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352), *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449), and *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-references, identifying 54 matching passages across ten Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, segments §12.4–15.4 of Pv 25 recur verbatim or near-verbatim in Ja 352, Ja 372, Ja 410, Ja 449, and Ja 454, as well as in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. The text also exhibits extensive internal reuse with its own commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (§0.3–6.6) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the threshold were detected in Sanskrit, Tibetan, or Chinese corpora [DharmaNexus].
